subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 48-year-old man has diabetes mellitus, hyperpigmentation, and cirrhosis. Serum transferrin saturation and ferritin are markedly elevated, and a liver biopsy shows iron deposits highlighted by Prussian blue stain.
question: Which of the following best describes the pathogenesis of his condition?

options.text: Autosomal recessive ATP7B mutation causing decreased biliary copper excretion
Autosomal recessive HFE mutation on chromosome 6 causing low hepcidin and increased intestinal iron absorption
Increased hepcidin production causing decreased intestinal iron absorption
Defective UDP-glucuronosyltransferase causing unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
Autoimmune lymphocytic destruction of lobular bile ducts

explanation_correct: Hereditary hemochromatosis is autosomal recessive, caused by mutations in the HFE gene on chromosome 6. This leads to abnormally low hepcidin production, increasing intestinal iron absorption. Iron accumulates in liver, pancreas, skin, heart, pituitary, and joints, and hemosiderin can be identified on MRI or biopsy with Prussian blue stain. Secondary iron overload can also result from chronic transfusion therapy, as in beta-thalassemia major.

explanation_incorrect.A: ATP7B mutation with decreased biliary copper excretion causes Wilson disease, not iron overload.
explanation_incorrect.C: Hemochromatosis involves low, not increased, hepcidin; high hepcidin would reduce intestinal iron absorption.
explanation_incorrect.D: Defective UGT causes unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (Gilbert or Crigler-Najjar), not iron overload.
explanation_incorrect.E: Lymphocytic destruction of lobular bile ducts is primary biliary cholangitis.

educationalObjective: HFE mutation on chromosome 6 lowers hepcidin and increases intestinal iron absorption, producing iron overload in hemochromatosis.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 55-year-old man presents with cirrhosis, newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus, and a bronzed hyperpigmentation of his skin.
question: Which of the following terms best describes this classic presentation?

options.text: Charcot triad
Reynolds pentad
Bronze diabetes
Courvoisier sign
Rigler triad

explanation_correct: Hereditary hemochromatosis classically presents after age 40, once total body iron exceeds about 20 g, with the triad of cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, and skin pigmentation known as bronze diabetes. Iron loss through menstruation slows progression in females. Hepatocellular carcinoma is a common cause of death in these patients.

explanation_incorrect.A: Charcot triad (jaundice, fever, RUQ pain) is seen in acute cholangitis.
explanation_incorrect.B: Reynolds pentad adds altered mental status and shock to Charcot triad in severe cholangitis.
explanation_incorrect.D: Courvoisier sign is a palpable, nontender gallbladder with obstructive jaundice in pancreatic cancer.
explanation_incorrect.E: Rigler triad (pneumobilia, bowel obstruction, gallstone) is seen in gallstone ileus.

educationalObjective: Bronze diabetes cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, and hyperpigmentation is the classic presentation of hemochromatosis after age 40.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 52-year-old woman with hemochromatosis develops exertional dyspnea and restricted ventricular filling on echocardiography. She also has pain and swelling of her metacarpophalangeal joints.
question: Which of the following best explains these findings?

options.text: Copper deposition in the myocardium and joints
Amyloid infiltration of the heart and joints
Iron deposition confined to the liver and pancreas
Iron deposition causing restrictive cardiomyopathy and calcium pyrophosphate arthropathy
Uric acid crystal deposition in the joints without cardiac involvement

explanation_correct: Hemochromatosis causes iron deposition in the heart, producing a classic restrictive cardiomyopathy (and a reversible dilated cardiomyopathy), and in the joints, causing arthropathy from calcium pyrophosphate deposition, especially at the metacarpophalangeal joints. Other manifestations include hypogonadism, skin pigmentation, and hepatocellular carcinoma.

explanation_incorrect.A: Myocardial and joint copper deposition occurs in Wilson disease, not hemochromatosis.
explanation_incorrect.B: Cardiac amyloidosis can cause restrictive physiology but is not the iron-driven, MCP-predominant calcium pyrophosphate arthropathy described here.
explanation_incorrect.C: Iron deposition is not confined to liver and pancreas; it also accumulates in heart, pituitary, skin, and joints.
explanation_incorrect.E: This is calcium pyrophosphate deposition, not monosodium urate gout, and cardiac iron involvement is central to the presentation.

educationalObjective: Hemochromatosis causes restrictive cardiomyopathy and calcium pyrophosphate arthropathy of the MCP joints from iron deposition.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 50-year-old man with hemochromatosis is found to have significant iron overload and requires treatment to remove excess iron.
question: Which of the following is an accepted treatment for this condition?

options.text: Penicillamine chelation
Oral zinc supplementation
Ursodiol
Phototherapy
Repeated phlebotomy or iron chelation with deferasirox, deferoxamine, or deferiprone

explanation_correct: Hemochromatosis is treated with repeated phlebotomy to remove iron-rich red blood cells. When phlebotomy is not tolerated or feasible, iron chelation with deferasirox, deferoxamine, or deferiprone can be used. This differs from Wilson disease, which is treated with copper chelators and zinc.

explanation_incorrect.A: Penicillamine is a copper chelator used in Wilson disease, not for iron overload.
explanation_incorrect.B: Zinc is used in Wilson disease to reduce copper absorption, not to remove excess iron.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ursodiol is used in primary biliary cholangitis to promote bile flow.
explanation_incorrect.D: Phototherapy is used for neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.

educationalObjective: Hemochromatosis is managed with repeated phlebotomy or iron chelators such as deferasirox, deferoxamine, and deferiprone.
